title: Maximum Difference Score in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, you can move to any cell directly below or to the right.
statement: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, you can move to any cell directly below or to the right. The score for moving from a cell with value c1 to a cell with value c2 is c2 - c1. Starting from any cell, make at least one move to maximize the total score.
constraints: grid is rectangular, positive-valued, and contains at least two cells.
From a cell, a move may go any positive distance down in the same column or right in the same row; make at least one move.
The scores telescope, so maximize final value minus starting value over reachable distinct cells.
hints: Any move sequence score telescopes to destination value minus start value; a valid start for (r,c) lies anywhere above or left.
Maintain the minimum value in the inclusive upper-left reachable region, but score before adding the current cell to enforce at least one move.
The prefix recurrence contains exactly all possible starts that can reach the current cell, so subtracting its minimum maximizes this destination’s score.
editorial: The prefix recurrence contains exactly all possible starts that can reach the current cell, so subtracting its minimum maximizes this destination’s score.

tests.explanation: Start at 5, move down to 7, then right to 14; the scores telescope to nine.
Every move decreases the value; moving from 10 to 8 gives the maximum score -2.
